slides.0.title: Regulatory Evolution and Diploma Reasoning
slides.0.subtitle: AOC promotion, denominations, organics and answer frameworks
slides.1.title: How AOCs evolved
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Promotion ladder
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Many areas climbed from vin de pays and VDQS to AOC, e.g. Coteaux Varois: 1974 vin de pays → 1984 VDQS → 1993 AOC
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Denominations
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Côtes de Provence denominations came from 2005 (Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe…), with Notre-Dame des Anges added in 2019
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The Trévallon case
slides.1.highlights.2.content: In 1993 Domaine de Trévallon left Les Baux AOC rather than accept the 20% Cabernet cap
slides.1.content: Promotion and denominations are tools for quality tiering.
slides.2.title: Answer framework
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Open with the point
slides.2.highlights.0.content: State a position, then natural factors, human factors and outcome
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Use specifics
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Support with numbers and names, e.g. Bandol's Mourvèdre at least 50% and 18 months in oak
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Flag uncertainty
slides.2.highlights.2.content: When sources disagree, say so instead of picking a number
slides.3.title: Sample prompts
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Prompt one
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Compare Bandol and Côtes de Provence in style and regulation
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Prompt two
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Explain climate change's effect on Provence rosé
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Prompt three
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Discuss the commercial value of Corsica's local grapes
slides.3.content: Practise with the framework, not memorised answers.
